http.description: Every enabled rule must pass against the same response. Response bodies are read only for body or JSON rules and are never stored.

http.jsonValue: Expected value (JSON, for example "ok", 0 or null)

latency.description_dns: DNS check time includes the DNS query and answer validation. It is not browser page-load performance. Disabled policies preserve existing behavior.
latency.description_tcp: TCP check time includes hostname resolution and connection establishment, not application authentication or browser page-load performance. Disabled policies preserve existing behavior.
latency.title: Latency and alert policy
latency.description: Request duration measures this HTTP check, not browser page-load performance. Disabled policies preserve existing behavior.
latency.rules: Every response assertion must pass. Invalid responses become Down after the failure threshold. Slow responses become Degraded after the configured count. Values between the two timing thresholds hold the current failing state and reset recovery progress.
latency.delivery: Critical and Warning use the selected channels. Informational keeps measured failures visible without paging. Enable degradation separately on each channel. Recovery goes only to destinations that received this failure; cooldown delays a new failure alert, while maintenance can delay it further.
latency.invalidRecovery: Recovery threshold must not exceed the slow threshold.
latency.testNote: This is one sample. It does not advance consecutive counts, create incidents or send alerts.

heartbeat.title: Job heartbeat
heartbeat.description: Track job arrivals, failures and unfinished runs. New is unobserved; Late and Down use the expected interval and grace.
heartbeat.name: Name
heartbeat.deadlines: The first arrival is due one interval after creation. At the due time the job is Late; at due time plus grace it is Down. A start does not restore health or postpone the deadline.
heartbeat.oneTime: The new token replaces the previous token immediately. Update your job with the new URL.
heartbeat.copyError: Copy failed. Reveal and copy the token manually.
heartbeat.example: Set PULSY_HEARTBEAT_TOKEN privately in the job environment, then send a success:
heartbeat.headerOnly: Use the Authorization header only. Never put the token in a URL, log, exported configuration or job output. Start and fail use the same path with /start or /fail.
heartbeat.rotateConfirm: Rotate the token? The previous token stops working immediately. Update the job configuration.
heartbeat.paused: Paused: deadline checks and alerts are stopped. Real received terminal events still record measured health; pausing itself never restores health.
heartbeat.noRuns: No started runs yet. Simple success pings need no run ID.
heartbeat.heartbeat_unfinished: Started job did not finish before its deadline
heartbeat.lastEvaluatedHint: When Pulsy last evaluated this heartbeat. Active heartbeats are evaluated at their configured interval, when a deadline passes, or on a terminal ping. Evaluation does not imply a ping was received.
heartbeat.stateNone: No heartbeat has been received yet. The first is due {{relative}} ({{absolute}}).
heartbeat.stateOnTime: On schedule. The next heartbeat is due {{relative}} ({{absolute}}).
heartbeat.stateLate: Late. It was expected {{relative}}; it counts as Down if nothing arrives by {{absolute}}.
heartbeat.stateOverdue: Overdue. The grace deadline passed {{relative}} ({{absolute}}) with no heartbeat since.
heartbeat.stateDown: Down. Pulsy keeps evaluating this heartbeat; only a successful ping restores health.
heartbeat.deadlineExample: A heartbeat is expected every {{interval}}. With {{grace}} of grace, Pulsy marks the job Down {{total}} after the previous one.
heartbeat.stateAwaitingSuccess: A ping was received, but no success yet. The first success is due {{relative}} ({{absolute}}).
heartbeat.rotateToReveal: Rotate the token in Settings to enable URL reveal and copying for this older heartbeat.
heartbeat.urlSecurity: This URL is a secret. Reveal it to use the examples; keep it out of logs, screenshots and shared files.
heartbeat.intervalHelp: How often the job should send a successful ping.
heartbeat.wholeSeconds: Use a duration that equals a whole number of seconds.

reliability.error: History could not be loaded or saved.
reliability.partial: Some boundary or retained data is unavailable; unknown time remains unknown.
reliability.utcDays: Daily rows use UTC dates. Coverage and missing data remain separate.
reliability.noAnnotations: No private markers in this window.
reliability.invalidWindow: Choose an end after the start.
reliability.measurement: Observations cover up to one recorded interval. Gaps and older uncaptured history stay unknown. Down and Degraded consume downtime; this duration-weighted view is separate from the check success ratio.
reliability.goalDescription: Blank targets disable the corresponding goal. Goals do not change health, alerts or SLA reports.
reliability.policyDescription: Changes create a measurement version. Captured maintenance adjustments remain separate from raw history; snooze never excludes time. Availability budgets compare against the current target; latency compliance uses captured versions.
reliability.sampleRatio: Successful checks: {{value}}. Captured samples: {{count}}. This is a sample ratio, not observed duration.
reliability.exportDescription: Exports this exact operational window and coverage. PDF reports and monthly SLA delivery are also available to every account.
reliability.annotationDescription: Private to the owner. Record correlation, not a proven cause. Use a timestamp within retained history and a link without credentials, query or fragment. Do not enter secrets.
reliability.policyVersion: Version {{version}} · {{date}} · availability {{target}} · latency {{latency}} ms · maintenance exclusion {{exclusion}}
reliability.publicDescription: Seven completed UTC days, loaded when expanded. Unknown gaps stay neutral. Raw availability, observed coverage and separately enabled maintenance adjustment are distinct. Request timing is not browser page-load performance.
reliability.incidentDescription: Incidents overlapping this window, with durations clipped to its boundaries. Cause totals sum incident durations; overlapping incidents can count simultaneously and do not define measured availability.
reliability.causesPartial: Cause summaries cover the newest 1,000 matching incidents only. Incident pages remain complete.
reliability.enableHistory: Show public history for this page
reliability.enablingHistory: Enable raw availability, coverage, typed timing and separate maintenance adjustment for these exact public components.
reliability.disablingHistory: Disable public history for this page.
reliability.historyDisclosure: This optional setting publishes availability and performance measurements for explicitly selected components. Private notes and goals stay private. Preview and apply before any change becomes effective.

creation.nameOptional: Optional. Uses the hostname when left empty.
creation.quickPolicy: Three consecutive failures open an incident. Timeout: 10,000 ms. HTTPS checks also inspect the TLS certificate.
creation.checkSummary: Every {{interval}} · Consecutive failures that open an incident: {{failures}} · Timeout: {{timeout}} (allowed 1,000–60,000 ms).
creation.policySummary: Slow when above {{threshold}} ms for {{slow}}; recover at or below {{recovery}} ms for {{healthy}}. {{importance}} · Cooldown: {{cooldown}}.
creation.recoverySummary: Recover after {{healthy}}. {{importance}} · Cooldown: {{cooldown}}. Slow-response detection is off.
creation.jsonDistinctions: JSON values are typed: 0, false, null and "" differ. “Exists” accepts a present null; a missing path fails. All configured rules must pass.
creation.requestBounds: Up to 20 headers; 4,096 characters per value. Request body: up to 65,536 UTF-8 bytes. Stored private values are never displayed.
creation.immutableType: A monitor’s type cannot be changed. Create another monitor to use a different check type.
creation.invalidUrl: Enter a website address, for example example.com or https://example.com.
creation.duplicateUrl: This URL is already monitored by “{{name}}”.

bulkUX.previewHelp: Valid entries will be submitted. Duplicate, invalid and unsupported entries are skipped.
bulkUX.atomic: The reviewed valid batch is created together. If the server rejects it, nothing is created and your input stays here.

historyUX.title: Check log
historyUX.scope: All retained observations, newest first. This log is independent of the reliability range above. Times: {{timezone}}.
historyUX.loadError: The check log could not refresh. Previously loaded rows remain available; retry with Refresh.
historyUX.markerTimezone: Private marker · {{timezone}}. Correlation does not establish a cause. These notes are never published.
historyUX.reportBasis: Check success is successful recorded checks divided by all recorded checks in this report window. Response statistics use recorded timings. Observed availability and coverage are in History.
historyUX.invalidLocalTime: Enter a valid, unambiguous time in {{timezone}}. Times skipped or repeated during clock changes cannot be used.

incidentUX.runbookChanged: The saved runbook changed while you were editing. Your draft is kept. Review the saved version below.
incidentUX.filteredEmpty: No incidents match these filters. Clear filters to broaden the results.
incidentUX.delaySummary: {{duration}} after incident start · eligible {{time}}. Allowed: 60–86,400 seconds.
incidentUX.resultMore: More results on the next page.

maintenanceUX.timezoneHelp: Choose a timezone or enter an IANA name, such as Europe/Berlin or America/New_York.
maintenanceUX.futureEdits: Only schedules that have not started can be edited. Cancel an existing recurrence and create a future schedule to change it without rewriting past maintenance.
maintenanceUX.editScope_one: This edit applies to the {{count}} monitor in the saved schedule.
maintenanceUX.editScope_other: This edit applies to all {{count}} monitors in the saved schedule.

notificationUX.recipientsHint: Separate addresses with commas. Duplicate destinations are sent once.
notificationUX.deleteChannel: Delete this channel? It will stop receiving alerts everywhere it is reused. Detach a template channel to remove it from only one monitor.
notificationUX.deleteProvider: Delete “{{name}}”? Channels and scheduled reports using this provider will need another provider.
notificationUX.providerTestDestination: Test sends to your account email address. Acceptance by a provider does not confirm receipt.
notificationUX.retainSecrets: Leave replacement credentials empty to retain the stored secret. Stored secrets are never shown.
notificationUX.historyScope: Recorded delivery attempts only. Queued and suppressed alerts appear in the incident timeline. Provider acceptance does not confirm human receipt.
notificationUX.errorChannels: Notification channels could not be loaded. Try again.
notificationUX.errorProviders: Email providers could not be loaded. Try again.
notificationUX.errorLog: Delivery history could not be loaded. Try again.
notificationUX.confirmTest: Send a real test alert to {{destination}}?
notificationUX.testAccepted: Test accepted by the provider for {{destination}}. Acceptance does not confirm delivery.
notificationUX.noProviderBody: Add an email provider here, then test it under Email providers before relying on delivery. Your channel draft stays open.
notificationUX.providerUntestedHint: This provider has not passed a test yet. Alerts may fail; send a test from Email providers.
notificationUX.tlsUnavailable: TLS certificate expiry alerts are not available for this monitor type.
notificationUX.reverifyHint: Changing the provider type or credentials marks the provider as not yet tested. Send a test after saving.
notificationUX.monitorScope: These channels alert only for this monitor. Account-wide defaults and template channels are listed separately and also apply.
notificationUX.emailExample: Enter email addresses such as alerts@example.com, separated by commas.
notificationUX.noEffectiveChannels: No effective channels are configured. Add a monitor channel or an account-wide default to enable alerts.
notificationUX.noAttempts: Channels are configured, but no delivery attempts are recorded. Delivery depends on enabled events, failure thresholds, suppression and provider readiness.
notificationUX.inheritedActive: Inherited or linked channels apply to this monitor. Add a channel here only for an additional destination.
notificationUX.telegramBotHelp: Enter the bot token from BotFather (for example 123456:ABC).
notificationUX.telegramChatHelp: Enter a numeric chat ID (including a leading minus for groups) or @channel.
notificationUX.telegramInvalid: Enter a bot token and a numeric chat ID or @channel.
notificationUX.defaultPolicy: Account-wide defaults always apply to every monitor, including newly created monitors. To limit recipients, configure channels on individual monitors instead of using account-wide defaults.
notificationUX.secretOnce: Save this secret now. It is shown only once. Rotating it immediately invalidates the previous secret.

statusUX.validationError: Review the highlighted fields and try again.
statusUX.stale: This page changed elsewhere. Your draft is retained. Reload the saved version before replacing it.
statusUX.deleteNamed: Delete “{{name}}”? Its public page and subscriptions will be removed. Monitors are kept.
statusUX.draftLimit: Draft pages have no public preview. Review names, disclosures and announcements here before publishing.
statusUX.requiredHint: Title and slug are required. Other text fields are optional.
statusUX.slugHint: Use 1–63 Latin letters or numbers separated by single hyphens. Surrounding spaces are trimmed and letters are saved in lowercase.
statusUX.optionalDescription: Optional. Displayed publicly, up to {{max}} characters.
statusUX.publishHint: Saving publishes this page at the URL shown. Selected component names and enabled disclosures become public.
statusUX.stalePublic: Refresh failed. Showing the last loaded observations; check their timestamps before relying on them.
statusUX.urlCopyFailed: Could not copy. Select the address and copy it manually.
statusUX.publishEmpty: This page has no components yet. Visitors will see “No monitors configured” until you add some.
statusUX.confirmEmptyPublication: This page has no components. Publish it with an empty status summary?
statusUX.unpublishConfirm: Unpublish “{{name}}”? Its public address will stop showing the page.
statusUX.defaultSlugHelp: The default address is read-only. Create another page to choose a different slug.
statusUX.emptyPublishedWarning: Published with no components. Add components so visitors can see their status.
statusUX.uptimeHint_one: Checks that answered correctly, including slow responses, out of all recorded checks in the last {{count}} day.
statusUX.uptimeHint_other: Checks that answered correctly, including slow responses, out of all recorded checks in the last {{count}} days.

shareUX.disclosure: Recipients can copy the HTTP settings shown in the preview into independent monitors. Secrets, history, incidents, notification channels, subscribers and public-page membership stay private. The link shows current safe settings until it expires or you revoke it.
shareUX.entryHint: Select monitors in the collection, then choose Share from the bulk actions. This does not publish a status page.
shareUX.repeatHint: Import starts new active checks. A URL you already monitor cannot be imported again: open your existing monitor instead. No history, tokens, private request values or notification recipients are copied.

server.title: Linux server
server.description: Monitor host CPU, RAM, filesystems and agent connectivity.
server.installDescription: Run one command on the Linux host. It downloads, verifies, configures and starts the agent. Without the one-time credential on screen, the installer asks for it at a hidden prompt. Linux amd64 and arm64 are supported.
server.commandContainsCredential: These commands include the one-time credential. Treat them like a password: they are saved in the shell history on the host.
server.oneTime: Save this credential now. It is shown only once. Rotation immediately revokes the previous credential.
server.httpsRequired: Configure a public HTTPS Pulsy origin before installing the agent.
server.composeStart: Docker Compose installation starts the container automatically. Read-only host mounts report host metrics.
server.copyError: Copy failed. Select and copy the value manually.
server.name: Server name
server.alertTiming: Alert after 3 consecutive violations; recover after 2 healthy reports. Missing reports cause an outage after 3 intervals.
server.exclusionsHelp: One absolute path per line; descendants are excluded too. Maximum 32 paths.
server.invalid: Enter a name, a valid interval, thresholds from 0 to 100, and valid absolute paths.
server.error: Could not load or save server data. Try again.
server.pending: Pending — waiting for the first report
server.awaitingHint: The agent reports every {{interval}}. This monitor stays Pending until the first report arrives. Installation steps and troubleshooting are on the Overview tab.
server.troubleshooting: No report yet. Check the service logs, HTTPS connectivity, credential and system clock. The monitor stays pending until its first report.
server.rotateConfirm: Rotation immediately disconnects the current agent. Update its protected configuration and restart it with the new credential.
server.noMetrics: Metrics appear after the first agent report. CPU requires two counter samples.
server.retention: Retention: {{days}} days. Up to 1,000 recent reports are displayed for this window.
server.noHistory: No reports in this time window.
server.chartLabel: CPU, RAM and maximum filesystem utilization over time, from 0 to 100 percent. A data table follows.
server.tableLimit: The table shows the 50 most recent displayed samples. Gaps mean unavailable measurements.
server.retention_one: Retention: {{days}} day. Up to 1,000 recent reports are displayed for this window.
server.retention_other: Retention: {{days}} days. Up to 1,000 recent reports are displayed for this window.

httpStatuses.invalid: Enter HTTP codes from 100 to 599, comma-separated codes, a class such as 2xx, or an ascending range such as 200–299.

egress.checkBlocked: Check blocked by this server's egress policy. Metadata and link-local addresses are always blocked.

checkErrors.dns_not_found: DNS lookup failed — domain not found (NXDOMAIN)
checkErrors.response_timeout_unknown: Timed out waiting for a response
checkErrors.tls_hostname_mismatch: TLS certificate does not match the hostname
checkErrors.redirect_rejected: Redirect rejected by the request policy
checkErrors.assertion_failed: Response did not match the configured checks
